bullets: Game 4 of a six-game balance-change video (deck-showcase format: every game uses a different list, so this deck comes from the per-game read, not a video consensus). Readable window t=799-989, clock 2:50 to the first seconds of overtime.

Piloted as a defence-first chip deck: Bomb Tower re-anchored at the same centred tile every rotation ([8, 10], [9, 10], [8, 10], [8, 11]), Berserker and Archers behind it, Magic Archer parked deep at [9, 4] and [7, 0], Tornado and Royal Delivery to clump and clear, and Wall Breakers sent alone almost every cycle (7 plays in 190 s).

Wall Breakers switch lanes to follow the opponent's commitment — left river tile [4, 14] at clock 2:47, left bridge [4, 15] at clock 1:23, right bridge [14, 15] at clock 0:27, the last of which coincides with the enemy right tower falling 4654 -> 3722 (t=944-950).

Goblinstein is used three ways in one game: split-lane at [10, 8] (clock 2:23), pre-built behind the king at [11, 1] with the board empty (clock 1:37), and inside the big defensive stack at [7, 10] (clock 1:11) — no ability activation readable.

Against the opponent's Miner / Ram Rider / Royal Ghost / Guards / Executioner bridge spam it traded roughly evenly: enemy left 4858 -> 3552 and enemy right 4858 -> 3722, against his own left 4858 -> ~1900 and right 4858 -> 4059, going into overtime with no result readable.

The commentary is balance-change narration throughout, not piloting advice; his one in-match line is "I'm actually having trouble yapping about the balance changes while defending here" (t=953-956), spoken at 0 elixir with three simultaneous threat warnings.

new_deck.rationale: Five of eight slots are defensive value cards (Bomb Tower, Tornado, Royal Delivery, Magic Archer, Goblinstein) feeding a 2-elixir chip win condition, which is control's defend-then-punish plan rather than a push deck's.
new_deck.why_it_works_md: The deck answers pushes with a centred Bomb Tower plus a clumping Tornado and Royal Delivery, so almost every defence is elixir-positive, and it converts that lead into repeated 2-elixir Wall Breakers rather than into a counter-push. At 3.25 average elixir it cycles fast enough to send Wall Breakers roughly once per rotation and to switch lanes as soon as the opponent commits, which is how the enemy right tower was chipped from 4654 to 3722 in this match while Ryley defended in the other lane. Goblinstein is the flexible piece: split across both lanes as a defensive anchor, or pre-placed behind the king to be ready for the next push. Its weakness shows up here too — a single spell and sustained Miner chip took his own left tower from 4858 to about 1900, because nothing in the list punishes an opponent who keeps trading at the bridge.
